title: How far is the point where the circle meets the line?
description: A circle of radius seven centimetres is drawn with centre D, and it meets the line l at a point. The video finds how far that point is from D. Keeko's doubt is about what the seven centimetres measures, and the video breaks it.
teaching_notes: One idea: every point of a circle is at the radius from its centre. Watch for students who read the compass opening as the width of the whole circle.

source: A circle of radius 7 cm is drawn with centre D, and it meets
video_script.why: A learner sees that a circle gathers all the points at one fixed distance from its centre, so any point where it meets a line is that far from the centre.
video_script.substitution: the book's circle of radius seven centimetres with centre D, meeting the line l at the point B
video_script.anchor: the book's circle with centre D and radius 7 cm, meeting the line l at a point
video_script.wrong_answer: the circle is seven centimetres across
video_script.wrong_move: reads the compass opening as the width of the whole circle and halves it
video_script.payoff_line: That point is seven centimetres from dee, and it is the required point bee.

final_answer.spoken: that point is seven centimetres from dee

maths_rules: every point of a circle is at the radius distance from the centre
the point where the circle meets l is 7 cm from D, and it is B
the circle is 14 cm across, since 7 + 7 = 14
video_script.design: The circle with centre D and the line l stay on the board. A thread of seven centimetres turns about D and touches the circle at many points, one of which is on the line.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the circle is seven centimetres across. Then the point is only three and a half centimetres from dee.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the compass opening is the radius, from the centre to the circle. The circle is fourteen centimetres across.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>The point is seven centimetres from dee.
